notes.summary: A proved throughout the declared parameter range: the ordinary type is admissible exactly when b<c. A shifted Green power supplies an actual strict witness in mutual ordinary type, including when c-b<alpha.
notes.detailedSummary: Set t=c-b and q_L=L^alpha-(L-G_p)^alpha. Then q_L~U and dd^c q_L>=-alpha L^(alpha-1)w1, with no point atom. Choosing L sufficiently large gives the strict representative bG_p+q_L. Conversely, canonically removing bG_p from any hypothetical competitor gives a positive residual current whose horizontal average is a positive measure of total mass t. Negative t is impossible, and t=0 contradicts the unbounded averaged residual. The residual type is unbounded and nonanalytic. Empty types receive no numeric mass infimum.
notes.text:
This is an unverified mathematical proof of A and the elementary local facts used below. Throughout dd^c=i∂∂bar/(2π), d^c=i(∂bar-∂)/(4π), and dd^c log|z|²=[0]. Put ω=w1+w2, t=c-b, β=t w1+a w2, and λ=w1∧w2. The target is Y=P1×P1, initially with identity resolution and background θ=c w1+a w2. For b=0, bG_p denotes the genuine identically zero function, including on D; no product 0·(-∞) is used. Competitors are the entire ordinary type, without normalization or a model-envelope restriction.

First establish the local smooth-background facts. If B+dd^c f>=0 for a smooth real form B, choose locally a smooth strictly psh potential k with dd^c k>=B. Then f+k is psh. On smaller balls its radial convolutions decrease to its canonical representative. For f_ε=(f+k)*ρ_ε-k,
B+dd^c f_ε=(B+dd^c f)*ρ_ε+B-B*ρ_ε>=-o(1)h.
Consequently holomorphic pullback preserves the current inequality whenever the pulled-back psh function is not identically -∞. This follows by decreasing psh convergence and distributional convergence. In particular a locally bounded potential restricts canonically to a curve with the pulled-back inequality. For bounded potentials, Bedford–Taylor decreasing continuity gives the products with smooth-background corrections. Adding o(1)h before taking products proves their positivity; the errors vanish because local current masses remain bounded.

A removal fact will be useful. Suppose f is defined off a closed analytic set A, is locally bounded above, and B+dd^c f>=0 there. Choose a local closed positive form K=dd^c k>=B. The psh function f+k extends canonically across A by the permitted removable-singularity theorem. Thus S=K+dd^c f is positive globally. The smooth signed form B-K has no coefficient-measure mass on A. On the complement S+B-K is positive by hypothesis; on A its matrix of coefficient measures is that of S and is positive. Hence B+dd^c f>=0 globally. Canonical quasi-psh functions agreeing almost everywhere agree everywhere: after adding a common smooth potential, their values are recovered by limits of ball averages. The same argument extends inequalities from the complement of an analytic set.

Place p at z=0 by an FS isometry. Then
w=dd^c log(1+|z|²), G_p=log(|z|²/(1+|z|²)), T=-G_p>=0.
For L>=1 define
q_L=L^α-(L-G_p)^α=L^α-(L+T)^α, η_L=αL^(α-1).
Concavity shows q_L-U is bounded; its limit at T=∞ is L^α-1. The function q_L is smooth off p and has canonical value -∞ at p. Off p,
dd^c q_L=-α(L-G_p)^(α-1)w+α(1-α)(L-G_p)^(α-2)dG_p∧d^cG_p.
Therefore dd^c q_L>=-η_L w.

There is no hidden point atom. The boundary flux is O(T^(α-1)), which tends to zero; boundary terms involving a smooth test-function derivative vanish because |z|T^α tends to zero. More explicitly, angular integration gives the pushforward identities
w=e^(-T)dT,
dG_p∧d^cG_p=(1-e^(-T))dT.
For F_L(T)=α(L+T)^(α-1)(1-e^(-T)), the off-point pushforward of dd^c q_L is -F_L'(T)dT. Both endpoint values of F_L are zero. Its integral is therefore zero, agreeing with distributional Stokes. In particular Cw+dd^c q_L is a positive finite measure of mass C and has no atom whenever C>=η_L. These calculations require no first moment.

If t>0, choose L large enough that η_L<t. The actual genuine potential
r0=bG_p+q_L
is mutually ordinarily equivalent to r=bG_p+U, and Poincaré–Lelong gives
θ+dd^c r0=b[D]+β+dd^c q_L
>= (t-η_L)w1+(min a)w2
>= εω,
where ε=min(t-η_L,min a)>0. This proves sufficiency for every 0<α<1, even when t<α. The background θ itself is strictly positive and thus big in the stipulated nonclosed sense.

Conversely, suppose a genuine θ-psh v~r exists. Off D put q=v-bG_p. Mutual comparison gives |q-U|<=M there, and v is locally bounded outside D. Off D,
β+dd^c q=θ+dd^c v>=0.
Take C>max(0,t,max a,α) and K=Cω. Since K>=β, canonical removal extends q across D. Its value there is -∞ because q~U uniformly. The removal fact gives R=β+dd^c q>=0 globally. Both q and G_p are locally integrable, and v=bG_p+q holds distributionally and with the genuine pole values.

Let qbar(x)=∫q(x,y)w(y), interpreted in L1. Off p, |qbar-U|<=M. Fiber integration of R∧w2 gives the positive measure
σ=t w+dd^c qbar
on the first sphere, whose total mass is t by distributional Stokes. Thus t>=0. If t=0, σ=0 and qbar is a harmonic distribution, hence a smooth harmonic function and constant on the sphere. This contradicts qbar~U and its divergence to -∞ near p. Therefore b<c is necessary. For b>=c the type is empty, and no numeric infimum or supremum is assigned.

Finally q_L is unbounded but has zero transverse logarithmic coefficient: q_L/log|z|² tends to zero. An analytic singularity on a transverse disc is either bounded or has a positive logarithmic coefficient, by factoring the least vanishing order of its holomorphic generators. Neither possibility is ordinarily equivalent to U. Thus the residual ordinary type is unbounded and nonanalytic. The same transverse argument excludes analytic singularities for the full type after its coefficient b is removed.

notes.summary: B proved over every rough competitor. Closed comparison establishes canonical divisorial removal and full auxiliary closed mass without energy assumptions. Exact optimization gives R_minus=2(c-b)min a and R_plus=2(c-b)max a.
notes.detailedSummary: For every v~r, write v=bG_p+q canonically. In the closed K=C(w1+w2) class, q and q_L have mutual ordinary order and analytic small unbounded locus D. The permitted BEGZ comparison, checked against its printed primary source, applies in degrees one and two. It proves that S=K+dd^c q has no coefficient-measure mass on D and that its non-pluripolar square has full mass. Smooth corrections yield the actual finite positive nonclosed measure and its integral. Fiber averaging reduces every mass to 2∫aσ, where σ is positive of mass c-b. Actual potentials with increasingly small singular tails concentrate σ at either extremum of a.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof of B using n1. Assume t=c-b>0. Every competitor is a genuine θ-psh v~r, including arbitrary rough fiber-dependent competitors. Canonical removal gives v=bG_p+q, q~U, q=-∞ exactly on D, local boundedness off D, and R=β+dd^c q>=0.

The sole non-elementary comparison used is expressly permitted in the assignment. Its exact public primary source was independently opened: Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, Acta Math. 205 (2010), 199–262, DOI 10.1007/s11511-010-0054-7, https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf . Theorem 1.16 and its printed proof occur on pp.217–218, zero-based PDF pages 18–19; Definition 1.2 occurs on p.204. The theorem compares non-pluripolar cohomology classes under ordinary order for cohomologous CLOSED positive currents with small unbounded locus on a compact Kähler manifold. A positive change of dd^c convention is absorbed by inverse rescaling of potentials, leaving the actual currents and their products unchanged. No source comparison for nonclosed currents is invoked.

Choose L with η_L<t and C>max(t,max a,η_L). Set K=Cω, S=K+dd^c q, S0=K+dd^c q_L. These are globally closed positive currents on the compact Kähler surface Y, cohomologous to K, with mutual ordinary order. Their small unbounded locus is the closed analytic divisor D, locally the complete pluripolar set {log|z|²=-∞}. They are locally bounded outside D. All comparison hypotheses are thereby verified.

For the separated reference, bounded locality away from D and the curve computation in n1 give the actual product
⟨S0²⟩=2C(Cw1+dd^c q_L)∧w2.
Its mass is 2C²=∫K². Its order-one current has no mass on D because the first-factor measure has no atom.

Apply the permitted comparison in degree one to S and S0 in both orders, then pair with K. This gives
∫⟨S⟩∧K=∫S0∧K=∫K².
Order-one locality gives ⟨S⟩=1_(Y\D)S. Since ∫S∧K=∫K² by distributional Stokes, the positive defect 1_D S has zero pairing with the strictly positive form K and must vanish. Thus S has no coefficient-measure mass on D. This establishes the needed divisorial-removal assertion without invoking a Siu decomposition or imposing an energy condition.

Apply the same comparison in degree two, with both entries equal to S and both reference entries equal to S0, again in both orders. It yields
∫⟨S²⟩=2C².
These comparisons involve only closed currents, never R or θ+dd^c v.

Put B=β-K. On Y\D, bounded products with smooth corrections give
MA_ext,β(q)=⟨S²⟩+2S∧B+B².                 (1)
The right side is a finite signed measure globally: its first term has mass 2C², S has finite coefficient masses, and B is smooth. Every term puts no mass on D. Off D it is positive by the local approximation in n1. Consequently it is a positive global measure, and locality identifies it with the actual extended non-pluripolar product. This also proves existence, finiteness, and independence of C. On Y\D the currents θ+dd^c v and β+dd^c q coincide; their non-pluripolar products both vanish on D. Their extended measures are therefore equal.

Integrating (1), using the full closed mass and distributional Stokes, gives
M(v)=∫β²+2∫dd^c q∧(β-K)
=2t∫a w+2∫q dd^c a∧w2.                  (2)
Only the L1 function q is integrated against smooth forms. No first moment against S or its Monge–Ampère measure appears.

With qbar and σ=t w+dd^c qbar from n1, formula (2) becomes
M(v)=2∫a σ.                              (3)
The measure σ is positive, has total mass t, and has no atom at p by the no-D-mass conclusion. Hence every mass is positive and finite, and
2t min a<=M(v)<=2t max a.                  (4)
This applies to all rough competitors through their actual fiber averages.

The requested original-background formula follows from dd^c θ=dd^c a∧w2 and
∫G_p dd^c θ=a(p)-∫a w.
Substituting v=bG_p+q into (2) yields
M(v)=∫θ²-2b a(p)+2∫v dd^c θ.
Its last integral is finite by local integrability of v and smoothness of the coefficient density. It generally depends on v; no nonclosed intersection invariance is asserted.

To prove exactness of the extrema, choose any first-factor point x0 and smooth strictly positive probability forms ξ_j converging weakly to δ_x0. Choose L_j tending to infinity with η_j=αL_j^(α-1)<t and η_j tending to zero. Define the smooth global Green potential
h_j(x)=(t-η_j)∫G_z(x)ξ_j(z).
The locally integrable logarithmic kernel and its smooth right-hand side give smoothness, and Poincaré–Lelong gives dd^c h_j=(t-η_j)(ξ_j-w). Set q_j=q_(L_j)+h_j and v_j=bG_p+q_j. Each q_j~U and
 t w+dd^c q_j=(t-η_j)ξ_j+(η_j w+dd^c q_(L_j))>=0.
The second positive summand has mass η_j and tends weakly to zero. Thus the horizontal measures converge to tδ_x0. The potentials v_j are actual θ-psh competitors in the exact ordinary type: their residual currents have the displayed nonnegative horizontal part and the positive vertical part a w2. By (3), their masses tend to 2t a(x0). Selecting minimizing and maximizing points proves
R_minus=2(c-b)min a,
R_plus=2(c-b)max a.
The ordinary-equivalence constants may depend on j; uniform constants are not part of optimization over an entire fixed type.

notes.summary: C proved for the actual product embedding. The exact ambient ideals are O(-floor(sb)(D×P1)), including integer boundary weights, and every intrinsic trace is b ord_E(pi*D).
notes.detailedSummary: Use r0=bG_p+q_L from n1 and the smooth target Y0=Y×{z0} in Z=Y×P1. The ambient potential is genuinely admissible and has generic Lelong number zero along Y0. A transverse germ of order k is integrable precisely when k+1>sb; equality fails because of the positive sublinear exponential. Restricting the resulting ambient coherent ideal and pulling back that invertible ideal gives the exact traces on every modification. The residual has trivial ideals at all real weights despite its unbounded nonanalytic ordinary type.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof of C using n1. Assume b<c and select L with η_L<c-b. Put r0=bG_p+q_L,
Z=Y×P1, Y0=Y×{z0}, Θ=pr_Y^*θ+w3, u_Z=pr_Y^*r0.
The background is smooth and strictly positive, and
Θ+dd^c u_Z=pr_Y^*(θ+dd^c r0)+w3>=0.
Thus this is an actual admissible ambient representative. If a is nonconstant, dΘ=pr_Y^*(da∧w2) is nonzero. The initial target resolution is the identity, with Θ|Y0=θ and u_Z|Y0=r0. At a generic point of Y0 the potential is smooth, so its generic Lelong number along Y0 is zero. Smooth positive volume densities are locally comparable, and their choice does not change integrability ideals.

Near D take a transverse coordinate z and T0=-log|z|². Since G_p=log|z|²+O(1), and bounded changes of the argument of x^α change it by a bounded amount for α<1,
u_Z=b log|z|²-T0^α+O(1).
For a nonzero holomorphic germ with transverse vanishing order k, write f=z^k F. The function F is bounded above on a smaller polydisc and bounded below on some open set of the remaining variables near z=0. Fubini therefore gives the exact integrability criterion from
∫_0^ε r^(2k-2sb+1)exp(s(-log r²)^α)dr
=(1/2)∫_(Tε)^∞ exp(-(k+1-sb)T+sT^α)dT.
Because T^α=o(T), this is finite exactly when k+1>sb. At equality the integrand is exp(sT^α) and diverges. Hence the least allowed nonnegative integer k is floor(sb). In particular, at sb=N an integer, order N-1 fails at the exact boundary and order N succeeds. This proves the normalization directly with |f|²exp(-su), without an additional factor 2.

Away from D×P1 the potential is locally bounded. The local calculations glue to
I(su_Z)=O_Z(-floor(sb)(D×P1))
for every real s>0. Boundedly equivalent representatives have the same ideals because their exponential factors are comparable above and below.

Now restrict this actual ambient coherent ideal. Its local divisor equation remains the equation of D on Y0, so
I(su_Z)O_Y0=O_Y0(-floor(sb)D).
For every smooth compact modification π:Y'→Y0 and every prime divisor E on Y', the invertible restricted ideal has order
floor(sb)ord_E(π^*D).
The divisor multiplicity is a finite nonnegative integer. Dividing by s and taking the prescribed limit gives
τ_(Y0,u_Z)(E)=b ord_E(π^*D).
This includes all prime divisors on all smooth compact modifications and does not require a normal-crossings total transform. Total transforms and their orders are compatible with composition. No equality is inferred from trace-envelope lower inequalities, and the restriction of the ambient ideal has not been replaced by a multiplier ideal of a pulled-back potential.

With b=0, the same integral is finite for k=0 at every real s>0. Therefore I(sq_L)=O_Y at every weight, and likewise on the ambient product. Nevertheless q_L is unbounded and its ordinary type is nonanalytic by n1. Ideal equality does not give ordinary equivalence and does not record α.

notes.summary: D proved for an actual admissible shifted residual and a closed dominating K. The separated product has full mass; its first moment is finite exactly for alpha<1/2, with logarithmic divergence at alpha=1/2.
notes.detailedSummary: The explicit angular density of Cw+dd^c q_L is (C-alpha(L+T)^(alpha-1))e^(-T)+alpha(1-alpha)(L+T)^(alpha-2)(1-e^(-T)). It has mass C and no atom, giving actual closed top mass 2C². Multiplication by -q_L produces a positive tail asymptotic to 2C alpha(1-alpha)T^(2alpha-2). This proves the finiteness threshold and divergence rates. A–C impose no finite-energy or first-moment condition.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof of D. Assume b<c, choose L with η_L<c-b, and take the actual β-psh residual q0=q_L~U. Choose C>max(c-b,max a,η_L) and K=C(w1+w2). The form K is closed and dominates β; it is an auxiliary Kähler form, not a replacement of the nonclosed target background.

By the separated curve computation of n1, the actual product is
MA_K(q0)=⟨(K+dd^c q0)²⟩=2C(Cw1+dd^c q_L)∧w2.
It has mass 2C²=∫K², so it has full closed mass.

Under T=-G_p, the angular pushforward of the positive first-factor measure has density
A(T)=(C-α(L+T)^(α-1))e^(-T)
+α(1-α)(L+T)^(α-2)(1-e^(-T)).
Its mass is C and it has no atom. Since -q0=(L+T)^α-L^α, the actual extended nonnegative first moment is
∫Y(-q0)MA_K(q0)
=2C∫_0^∞[(L+T)^α-L^α]A(T)dT.
It is finite on bounded intervals. Its exponentially decaying part is integrable for every 0<α<1. The remaining positive tail is asymptotic, with ratio tending to one, to
2Cα(1-α)T^(2α-2)dT.
Comparison with power integrals proves finiteness exactly when α<1/2. At α=1/2 the truncation at T=R diverges as (C/2)log R. For α>1/2 it diverges as
[2Cα(1-α)/(2α-1)]R^(2α-1).
The logarithm refers to the T cutoff; for a radius cutoff this is a double logarithm.

Together with n1–n3, this establishes that all their admissibility, mass, and ideal conclusions hold throughout 0<α<1, including these actual infinite-moment examples. The closed full-mass comparison in n2 did not assume a finite moment.

Observational evidence is reproducible with python artifacts/check_s11.py > artifacts/check_output.json. For C=4,L=16, truncated moments at R=100,10^4,10^6 were approximately (1.034980,1.174376,1.197483) for α=1/4; (5.214753,12.805760,21.869063) for α=1/2; and (21.669737,279.770695,2976.274596) for α=3/4. These observations illustrate, but do not prove, the analytic tail laws. No resource-heavy computation was needed.

notes.summary: E proved: smooth gauges and pure modifications preserve competitors, actual non-pluripolar pushforward, optimized masses and intrinsic trace transport. A point blowup outside D has an explicit one-sided strict witness and no mutual-type strict witness.
notes.detailedSummary: Canonical descent across the analytic exceptional image gives an inverse to pullback for the entire competitor family. Locality on the biholomorphic complements and zero non-pluripolar mass on analytic sets prove the actual pushforward law, upstairs finiteness, and equality of both optimized masses. Trace transport uses total transforms of the original restricted ambient ideals. On a point blowup outside D, adding a small cutoff logarithmic pole to the pullback of r0 yields a smooth positive residual form plus an exceptional divisor. A mutual-type witness would be bounded near the exceptional curve, whose canonical restriction contradicts Stokes because the pure background restricts to zero.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof of E using n1–n3. Assume b<c. On a smooth modification π:Y'→Y, the declared target is Y' with PURE background π^*θ and ordinary type [π^*r]. Pullback means the actual canonical holomorphic pullback, including pole values.

For a real smooth f, set θ'=θ+dd^c f, r'=r-f, v'=v-f. This is a bijection of competitor families preserving ordinary comparisons, and θ'+dd^c v'=θ+dd^c v. Bounded products and their non-pluripolar extensions give the same actual extended measures, hence identical infima and suprema. The factor exp(sf) is locally bounded above and below by positive constants, so all real-weight ideals, their ambient restrictions, and intrinsic traces are unchanged. On the product ambient space use the gauge pr_Y^*f. Big positivity is preserved by the current equality.

For pure modifications, choose proper closed analytic sets A⊂Y and A'⊂Y' such that π is biholomorphic between their complements. These may include all exceptional sets. Pullback preserves smooth-background current positivity by the local approximation in n1 and preserves the two ordinary inequalities.

Conversely, let v' be any genuine π^*θ-psh potential with v'~π^*r. Descend it on Y\A using the biholomorphism. Its ordinary bounds against r make it locally bounded above near A. Add a local smooth potential of a closed positive form dominating θ, and extend the resulting psh function canonically across A. The extensions agree on overlaps by almost-everywhere equality and canonicity. The removal argument of n1 proves θ+dd^c v>=0 globally. Both ordinary inequalities extend using ball averages after adding a common smooth potential to v and r. Thus v~r with the genuine values at poles. Its canonical pullback agrees almost everywhere with v', hence everywhere. Pullback and descent are inverse bijections, even before quotienting by constants. No factorization of the modification or Kähler assumption on Y' was used.

On the biholomorphic complements, bounded products with smooth corrections commute with coordinate changes, and non-pluripolar locality passes this to the actual measures. These products put no mass on proper analytic sets: off the poles this follows from bounded Bedford–Taylor products, and at the poles from the non-pluripolar construction. Smooth corrections have the same property. Therefore the upstairs measure has no mass on A', and its mass on the complement equals the downstairs mass on Y\A. The latter is finite by n2, which also proves global finiteness upstairs. Consequently the actual Borel-measure identity is
π_*MA_ext,π^*θ(π^*v)=MA_ext,θ(v).
The competitor bijection now gives
R_minus(π^*θ,[π^*r])=2(c-b)min a,
R_plus(π^*θ,[π^*r])=2(c-b)max a.

For trace transport, the original restricted ambient ideals of n3 are O_Y(-floor(sb)D). Their total transforms on Y' are O_Y'(-floor(sb)π^*D). Thus for every further modification ρ:Y''→Y' and prime F,
τ(F)=b ord_F(ρ^*π^*D).
This is the same intrinsic system indexed by divisors over Y. It does not assert I(sπ^*r0)=π^*I(sr0), nor replace the original ambient restricted ideals by new pulled-back multiplier ideals. Exceptional curvature subtraction is a different background operation, across which no equality is asserted. No invariance of V_μ for arbitrary upstairs densities is claimed.

Now declare π:Bl_yY→Y to be the point blowup at y∈Y\D, with exceptional curve E. Its lower optimized mass is positive by the preceding calculation. An actual one-sided strict witness can be constructed as follows.

Take r0 from n1 with θ+dd^c r0>=εω. Choose a coordinate ball about y whose closure misses D and a smooth radial cutoff χ equal to one on a smaller ball and zero outside a larger one. Define
h=χ log(|z1|²+|z2|²), h(y)=-∞,
extended by zero outside the chart. It is a genuine global quasi-psh function, bounded above. Its negative curvature is confined to the cutoff annulus and bounded below by -Mω. In the inner ball its logarithm is psh.

Let H=π^*h. In the blowup chart z1=s,z2=sξ near E,
H=log|s|²+log(1+|ξ|²),
dd^c H=[E]+η,
η=dd^c log(1+|ξ|²).
Globally η=dd^c H-[E] is a smooth closed form. On E it is the positive FS form. At E, π^*ω is positive in the normal direction and zero in the tangent direction. Therefore ε π^*ω+δη is strictly positive at E for every δ>0. In the inner ball away from E it is positive because the logarithmic curvature is nonnegative and π^*ω is positive. On the cutoff annulus η>=-Mπ^*ω, so 0<δ with δM<ε ensures positivity there. Outside the chart it equals ε π^*ω. Hence
A_δ=ε π^*ω+δη
is an actual smooth strictly positive form on the blowup. The genuine potential
w=π^*r0+δH
satisfies
π^*θ+dd^c w>=A_δ+δ[E]>=A_δ.
Since H is bounded above and r0~r, w<=π^*r+C. Its added exceptional pole prevents claiming mutual comparison, and it is not asserted to have the original exact ideal trace at E.

Suppose instead that a genuine strict witness v'~π^*r existed, with π^*θ+dd^c v'>=ε' h' for ε'>0 and a smooth Hermitian h'. Because r is smooth near y, mutual comparison makes v' bounded near E. Its canonical restriction to E is finite and bounded. The restriction argument of n1 gives
dd^c(v'|E)>=ε' h'|E,
since π^*θ|E=0. Distributional Stokes gives zero total integral on the left and a positive one on the right, a contradiction. Thus every mutual-type strict witness is excluded.

notes.summary: F proved for the explicitly declared all-test normalization: V_mu(beta)=2(c-b)/H with actual attainment. The derivative and integrated subtraction identity use the actual minimizer and are separate from R_plus.
notes.detailedSummary: Define D_mu(T)=∫sqrt(T²/mu)mu and V_mu(B)=inf(∫B∧T/D_mu(T))² over all smooth positive dd^c-closed tests. Fiber integration makes the averaged vertical coefficient a positive constant k. With A=∫a x, determinant positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz give D²<=2AkH, while the numerator is tk+A. The identity (tk+A)²-4tkA=(A-tk)² proves the all-test bound. The specified positive closed test attains every equality. Differentiating the exact formula proves the claimed subtraction pairing and its integrated identity on any compact positive segment, for constant d and smooth first-factor e.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof of F. Since V_μ and D_μ were not otherwise defined in the input, declare their all-test normalization explicitly:
D_μ(T)=∫Y sqrt(T²/μ)μ,
V_μ(B)=inf_(T smooth real (1,1), T>0, dd^c T=0)(∫Y B∧T/D_μ(T))².
Here T²/μ is the positive density ratio, with no inserted factorial. These are the functional and normalization for which F's formulas are proved. No PDE normalization or separated-test restriction is assumed.

Put t=c-b>0, μ=mλ, ∫m w=1, H=∫(m/a)w. Take any allowed test T. In local product-unitary frames write its Hermitian matrix as [[x,z],[conjugate(z),y]], so x,y>0 and
T²=2(xy-|z|²)λ.
The coefficients x,y and |z|² are globally well-defined. The smooth function k(x1)=∫y(x1,x2)w(x2) is the fiber integral of T. Differentiation under the integral and Stokes give dd^c k=0 from dd^c T=0. Thus k is a positive constant. This applies to arbitrary mixed and fiber-dependent tests.

Set A=∫a x λ>0. The numerator is N=tk+A. Determinant positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz give
D_μ(T)=∫sqrt(2m(xy-|z|²))λ
<=sqrt(2)∫sqrt(a x)sqrt(m y/a)λ,
D_μ(T)²<=2A∫(m y/a)λ=2AkH.
Consequently
N²/D_μ(T)²>=(tk+A)²/(2AkH)>=2t/H,
where the last inequality is (A-tk)²>=0. This proves the lower bound for every allowed test.

Let V=2t/H and define
g=Vm/(2a), T0=(g/a)w1+w2=(Vm/(2a²))w1+w2.
This test is smooth and strictly positive. It is actually closed because its first coefficient depends only on the first factor. It has k=1, z=0 and A=(V/2)H=t. Also
T0²/μ=V/a²,
D_μ(T0)=sqrt(V)H,
∫β∧T0=2t.
It attains the bound. Therefore V_μ(β)=2(c-b)/H. The identical argument with t replaced by c gives V_μ(θ)=2c/H.

For nonconstant a, replacing m=1 by m_ε=1+ε(1/a-∫(1/a)w), for sufficiently small nonzero ε, preserves positivity and normalization while changing H by ε times the positive variance of 1/a. Hence V_μ can depend on μ. The optimized masses in n2 do not. For strictly positive m and nonconstant a,
1/max a<H<1/min a,
so R_minus<V_μ(β)<R_plus. For constant a these residual values coincide.

Fix b,m, a real constant d, and a fixed smooth real first-factor function e. On any compact segment where t_s=c-sd-b>0 and a_s=a-se>0 everywhere, put
H_s=∫m/a_s w, V_s=2t_s/H_s,
T_s=(V_s m/(2a_s²))w1+w2.
This is the actual attaining test at every s. Differentiation is justified by uniform positivity on the compact segment. With J_s=∫m e/a_s² w,
H_s'=J_s, t_s'=-d,
(d/ds)sqrt(V_s)=-[d+(V_s/2)J_s]/[sqrt(V_s)H_s].
But
∫(d w1+e w2)∧T_s=d+(V_s/2)J_s,

Thus the claimed identity holds with the actual minimizer:
(d/ds)sqrt(V_μ(β_s))=-∫(d w1+e w2)∧T_s/D_μ(T_s).
Integrating from s0 to s1 gives
sqrt(V_μ(β_s0))-sqrt(V_μ(β_s1))
=∫_(s0)^(s1)[∫(d w1+e w2)∧T_s/D_μ(T_s)]ds.
It is a signed subtraction identity for the allowed signed d,e; it is nonnegative for pointwise nonnegative subtraction. It is not a derivative of R_plus and makes no assertion about arbitrary positive upstairs densities.

notes.text:
This final note claims a complete unverified solution of the restricted A–G assignment, with the all-test normalization explicitly declared in n6. It does not claim a solution of unrestricted original S11.

Declare c=1, b=1/4, α=3/4, a=2+τ, m=1 on Y=P1×P1, where the spherical height τ has distribution dτ/2 on [-1,1]. Take D={p}×P1, θ=w1+(2+τ)w2, β=(3/4)w1+(2+τ)w2, and μ=w1∧w2. The genuine ambient embedding is Y0=Y×{z0} in Z=Y×P1, with Θ=pr_Y^*θ+w3. Use the identity resolution initially and pure backgrounds on modifications. Since dτ∧w2 is not identically zero, θ, β and Θ are genuinely nonclosed, as are their pure pullbacks on the dense biholomorphic locus. None is identified with line-bundle curvature.

The actual potentials
q16=8-(16-G_p)^(3/4),
r0=(1/4)G_p+8-(16-G_p)^(3/4)
have η16=(3/4)16^(-1/4)=3/8. By n1,
θ+dd^c r0>=(3/8)w1+(2+τ)w2>=(3/8)(w1+w2).
Their genuine pole values on D are -∞, and r0 is mutually ordinarily equivalent to the specified r. This is an actual strict-current witness.

Since min a=1 and max a=3, n2 gives the exact entire-type optimized masses
R_minus=2(3/4)·1=3/2,
R_plus=2(3/4)·3=9/2.
These are not identified with the mass of the single displayed representative. All rough competitors have positive finite masses, and actual same-type sequences approach both bounds.

The declared height distribution gives
H=(1/2)∫_(-1)^1(2+τ)^(-1)dτ=(log3)/2.
Therefore the attained all-test values of n6 are
V_μ(β)=3/log3,
V_μ(θ)=4/log3.
For u_Z=pr_Y^*r0, the exact ambient-ideal calculation of n3 gives
τ_(Y0,u_Z)(E)=(1/4)ord_E(π^*D)
on every prime divisor on every smooth compact modification π of Y0.

Choose the auxiliary CLOSED form K=4(w1+w2), which dominates β. By n4 the actual separated closed product of q16 has full mass 32 but
∫(-q16)MA_K(q16)=∞.
Its tail is asymptotic to (3/2)T^(-1/2)dT, so the truncation grows as 3sqrt(R). This auxiliary K is expressly separate from the genuinely nonclosed target backgrounds.

For any declared point blowup π:Bl_yY→Y with y outside D, n5 preserves both optimized masses, 3/2 and 9/2. It gives the actual one-sided strict potential
w=π^*r0+δπ^*(χ log(|z1|²+|z2|²)),
with a chart missing D and sufficiently small positive δ. Its current dominates the explicit smooth positive form constructed in the blowup charts, and w<=π^*r+C. No mutually equivalent strict potential exists, by canonical restriction to the exceptional curve and Stokes. The new witness's added exceptional singularity is not asserted to have the original exact trace on that divisor.

The restricted invariant is the pair of existing whole-ordinary-type optimized masses of this actual target restriction. Here it is finite, gauge invariant, pure-modification invariant and positive precisely in the admissible unbounded family b<c. Its proved relation to the intrinsic data is τ(D)=b and the formulas 2(c-τ(D))min a and 2(c-τ(D))max a. It is not a complete trace invariant: fixing b and the background while varying α gives mutually inequivalent unbounded residual ordinary types with identical all-weight residual ideals, intrinsic traces and optimized mass pairs. No trace-envelope exactness or universal ambient/restricted mass equality has been assumed.

Coverage is complete within the restricted assignment: n1 proves A for every b>=0 and 0<α<1, including c-b<α and empty-type exclusion; n2 proves B over all rough competitors; n3 proves C from actual ambient ideal restrictions on every modification; n4 proves D without an energy hypothesis; n5 proves the gauges, pure-pullback laws and both distinct blowup strictness conclusions; n6 proves the all-test lower bound, attainment and actual subtraction formula; this note proves G and assembles the result.

Reproducibility: the unchanged input is input.json. The full proof artifacts are artifacts/proof_notes.md and artifacts/notes.json; the exact public-source audit is sources/verification.md. Run python artifacts/check_s11.py > artifacts/check_output.json. The checks used Python 3.12.14, SymPy 1.14.0 and mpmath 1.3.0 on Linux x86_64. All script assertions passed. They verified the symbolic derivative and algebraic square identity, computed H=0.54930614433405484569762261846126285, V_beta≈2.73071767988051218 and V_theta≈3.64095690650734957, checked truncated curve masses against exact boundary-flux corrections, and reported the moment and subtraction observations in n4 and n6. artifacts/deliverable_audit.json records an acyclic support graph and input SHA-256 a1ed701818e86136072573a753f624c09a43dff76c5a6ab347a09ec5eed3f89c. These computations are observations and algebra checks, not exhaustive enumerations or mathematical certification. No resource-heavy computation was launched.

Unrestricted S11 remains open for arbitrary nonclosed backgrounds, singular targets and general intrinsic trace systems. This family does not establish a general strict-current criterion from positive nonclosed restricted mass. No priority claim is made for the known definitions, divisorial principles or pure-pullback laws.
